Subject: Liability cap carve-out request: confidentiality / trade secrets

Hi Rachel / Lauren,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed with Ken and our legal team, Veridian needs explicit carve-outs to the liability cap in the MSA for: (1) proven exfiltration of Veridian trade secrets; and (2) unauthorized disclosure of highly confidential data (PII combined with model inputs). We understand Redwood's standard position, but given the sensitivity of our clinical models and the potential downstream patient risk, our counsel is asking for:

- An exclusion to the liability cap for damages resulting from an unauthorized disclosure of trade secrets, defined as per California Uniform Trade Secrets Act (CUTSA) language;
- A narrow exception to allow recovery of reasonable forensic investigation costs and actual remediation costs in excess of the cap when a qualifying confidentiality breach is proven;
- A contractual commitment to preserve evidence and provide a root-cause summary within a defined SLA (30 days) to enable our regulators to proceed.

Attached are redlines from our outside counsel (PDF). Can your legal team propose a mutually acceptable remediation/forensics path and sample language? Also please confirm whether Redwood would accept a carve-out limited to wilful misconduct or if you require a lower threshold.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
Veridian Labs

Quick answers up front: Redwood generally resists open-ended, unlimited damage carve-outs. In past deals we’ve accepted: (a) carve-outs for documented trade secret exfiltration tied to wilful misconduct or gross negligence, and (b) reimbursement of documented forensic costs up to a defined cap or on a carve-out basis if tied to the confirmed breach. We are open to discussing a short SLA for initial reporting and a commitment to cooperate with forensic vendors.

I’ll ask Legal to propose language that balances your concerns with our enterprise risk tolerances. Rachel

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Liability cap carve-out request: confidentiality / trade secrets

Marta — appreciate the specifics and the redlines. I reviewed Veridian's proposed CUTSA-style definition; below is an initial compromise draft we can live with as a starting point. Please note these are legal-to-legal negotiating points and not a final position.

Proposed language (for discussion):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the liability cap set forth in Section X shall not apply to (i) proven misappropriation of Customer Trade Secrets by Supplier (as defined below) resulting from Supplier's willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (ii) documented third-party exfiltration of Customer Trade Secrets where Supplier has failed to implement materially the Security Controls described in Schedule A, and Supplier's failure was the proximate cause of the exfiltration.

For purposes of this Section, 'Customer Trade Secrets' means information that: (a) derives independent economic value from not being generally known; (b) is the subject of reasonable measures to maintain its secrecy; and (c) is identified in writing by Customer as trade secrets prior to disclosure or discovered and documented during the incident for the purpose of remediation.

In the event of a qualifying confidentiality breach, Supplier shall: (A) promptly preserve forensic evidence and, where reasonably requested by Customer, permit Customer's retained forensic firm (subject to Supplier's reasonable security review) to access log data and system snapshots under a narrowly tailored non-disclosure agreement; (B) provide an initial root-cause summary within thirty (30) calendar days of Supplier's determination that a qualifying breach occurred; and (C) reimburse documented, reasonable third-party forensic investigation costs and documented remediation expenses. Reimbursement under (C) shall be: (1) paid in addition to the liability cap only to the extent such costs are explicitly documented and reasonably incurred; and (2) limited to two times the amount of documented forensic and remediation costs unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Key negotiation points we anticipate:
- Threshold: Customer wants a lower threshold (any disclosure) — we need willful misconduct/gross negligence or explicit Supplier failure to maintain controls.
- Automatic access: Customer wants immediate use of their forensic vendor; we need to require supplier's review and NDAs/timeboxed access for security reasons.
- Payment beyond cap: We are willing to make forensic/remediation costs carve out of the cap if narrowly tailored and documented; unlimited consequential damages remain excluded.

Lauren / Marissa: can you confirm whether Sales is willing to accept the two-times forensic cost limiter above, and whether Commercial wants to trade that for a 6-month service credit or a modest discount if Veridian requires immediate escalation/retainer coverage?

Vivek
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks for the thoughtful draft. Sales/Commercial input below:

- Two times the documented forensic/remediation costs as an upper bound is acceptable for this deal if Veridian also agrees to: (a) a narrow definition of 'Customer Trade Secrets' (customer has to identify material portions in writing within 30 days), and (b) a waiver of punitive/consequential damages claims and no class actions related to the same incident.
- In exchange, we can offer a 6-month service credit (10% of monthly committed spend), payable if a qualifying breach occurs and Supplier is found to be at fault per the defined threshold. That credit would be in addition to the documented remediation reimbursement (not a substitute).
- We prefer to keep the root-cause SLA at 30 days but can add an interim 10-business-day acknowledgement with a status update.

If Legal confirms the final wording, I can present the commercial trade-off to Veridian during the exec call.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

Vivek / Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. Veridian can accept the willful misconduct / gross negligence threshold plus the Supplier-failure carve-out in (ii), provided the Customer Trade Secret identification step is not used to unreasonably exclude data discovered post-incident. We need the forensic vendor access to be timely; requiring a multi-week security review for every request will defeat the purpose. Proposed compromise: Customer may engage its certified forensic partner immediately upon Supplier's written acknowledgment that a qualifying breach is suspected; Supplier's security review of the partner would be limited to 3 business days and cannot be used to deny access.

On remediation reimbursement caps: we prefer no artificial multiple cap (e.g., 2x) so long as costs are documented and limited to reasonable, customary fees. However, we can accept a commercial trade (the 10% service credit) if Redwood provides the 6-month credit up-front as a contingent line item in the order form (escrowed or contractually reserved).

We will circulate a clean redline based on Vivek's text and these commercial caveats. Appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
Marta
